script: Same multiplication. Python: 13 seconds. NumPy: two milliseconds.
Every layer of a neural network is one matrix multiplication: inputs times weights. Here, two 512 by 512 matrices: 134 million multiply-adds.
Plain Python does them one at a time. It takes 13.4 seconds.
NumPy hands the same job to compiled code that does many multiply-adds per instruction. On one core: 5 milliseconds.
On all 4 cores: 2.3 milliseconds. The same answer, almost 6 thousand times faster.
The million-weight network from the backpropagation video: one forward pass is three of these. NumPy: 10 milliseconds. Plain Python: about 40 seconds.
That's why AI runs on matrix multiplication. It's the one job computers have learned to do absurdly fast, and GPUs take it to thousands of cores.
